key_insight: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials can help screen crystallographic entries for physical plausibility, but their reliability is model-dependent and no single model catches all error types.
engineering_relevance: For large materials databases, MLIP-based relaxation offers a scalable validation layer that can flag suspect structures faster than manual expert review, improving data curation workflows.
method: Filtered 522,086 COD entries down to 317,457 high-quality structures.
Relaxed the structures with M3GNet and used convergence plus volume change as screening criteria.
Compared M3GNet, CHGNet, PET-MAD, and PET-OAM on 524 manually selected cases to probe failure modes.
evidence_signal: In the full COD set, 314,153 of 317,457 filtered structures (99.0%) relaxed without a large cell-volume change, while manual review of 327 structures showed no single descriptor threshold cleanly separates valid from invalid entries.
watch_item: Model-specific distortions and missed error types mean MLIP relaxation should be used as a multi-model screening aid, not a standalone validator.
paper_title: Assessing the Reliability of Foundational Machine Learning Potentials for Evaluating the Veracity of the Crystallography Open Database
